To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 100 kW IOT can be coupled to a superconducting structure with an effective Qext of 3×10 to meet power demands of less 1 kW/m for free electron lasers or those based on an energy recovery linac.
a high Q external tuner system can be designed that will meet the power and efficiency requirements of the next generation of RF accelerators.
a superconducting RF structure with an accelerating gradient of 25 MV/m, a Qext of 3×10^7, and a shunt impedance of 10^7 ohm/m can be efficiently powered by a single 10 kW IOT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and optimization of a RF amplifier system that is capable of efficiently delivering 300 W of power to a superconducting structure operating at 1.3 GHz.
the design of a RF system for superconducting structures that is optimized for low loss, high accelerating gradient and low power consumption.
the development of a high power amplifier system that is suitable for use with low loss, superconducting RF structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of IOT amplifiers with external tuner circuits is an attractive option for the future of high gradient accelerators.

the use of a high Qext external tuner with a solid state or IOT amplifier will allow the use of a superconducting structure to achieve accelerating gradients in excess of 20 MV/m with a power consumption of less than 300 W/m for beam currents up to 10 uA.
the RF power amplifier is a key element in the design of an RF system for superconducting cavities and the choice of the amplifier is a critical decision in this regard.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RF power requirements of future high gradient superconducting structures are modest and can be met by existing technology.
a high gradient, high efficiency RF system can be developed for use with a superconducting structure.
we have developed an RF system that is capable of meeting the power demands of the next generation of superconducting accelerators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RF losses associated with the tuner system are not significant for the power levels of interest.
it is possible to achieve high accelerating gradients in superconducting cavities with extremely low power requirements.
a low loss RF system is feasible and can meet the requirements for high gradient superconducting accelerators.
